arxiv-2104-01378.title: speechocean762: An Open-Source Non-native English Speech Corpus For Pronunciation Assessment
arxiv-2104-01378.creator: Junbo Zhang, Zhiwen Zhang, Yongqing Wang, Zhiyong Yan, Qiong Song, Yukai Huang, Ke Li, Daniel Povey, Yujun Wang
arxiv-2104-01378.description: Abstract This paper introduces a new open-source speech corpus named “speechocean762” designed for pronunciation assessment use, consisting of 5000 English utterances from 250 non-native speakers, where half of the speakers are children. Five experts annotated each of the utterances at sentence-level, word-level and phoneme-level.

arxiv-2104-08904.title: Autonomous Situational Awareness for UAS Swarms Thanks: 978-1-7281-7436-5/21/ $ 31.00 \$31.00 ©2021 IEEE
arxiv-2104-08904.creator: Vincent W. Hill, Ryan W. Thomas, Jordan D. Larson
arxiv-2104-08904.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Vincent W. Hill, Ryan W. Thomas, Jordan D. Larson. This paper describes a technique for the autonomous mission planning of unmanned aerial system swarms. Given a swarm operating in a known area, a central command system generates measurements from the swarm. If those measurements indicate changes to the mission situation such as target movement, the swarm planning is updated to reflect the new situation and guidance updates are broadcast to the swarm.

arxiv-2302-01239.creator: David E. Trilling, Michael Gowanlock, Daniel Kramer, Andrew McNeill, Brian Donnelly, Nat Butler, John Kececioglu
arxiv-2302-01239.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by David E. Trilling, Michael Gowanlock, Daniel Kramer, Andrew McNeill, Brian Donnelly, Nat Butler, John Kececioglu. We present here the design, architecture, and first data release for the Solar System Notification Alert Processing System (SNAPS). SNAPS is a Solar System broker that ingests alert data from all-sky surveys. At present, we ingest data from the Zwicky Transient Facility (ZTF) public survey, and we will ingest data from the forthcoming Legacy Survey of Space and Time (LSST) when it comes online.

arxiv-2504-19090.creator: H. Atmacan, M. Belhorn, Y. Guan, L. Li, B. Pal, S. Sandilya, A. J. Schwartz, B. Wang, S. Watanuki, M. Andrew, M. Barrett, M. Bessner, T. E. Browder, J. Bynes, J. arxiv-2504-19090.description: Abstract We report on the construction, operation, and performance of the Time-of-Propagation detector with imaging used for the Belle II experiment running at the Super-KEKB e + ​ e − e^{+}e^{-} collider. This detector is located in the central barrel region and uses Cherenkov light to provide particle identification among hadrons.

arxiv-2601-09611.title: Spatial Wilson Loops and Energy Loss for Heavy Quarks in Magnetized HQCD Model
arxiv-2601-09611.creator: Irina Ya. Aref’eva, Ali Hajilou, Kristina Rannu, Pavel Slepov
arxiv-2601-09611.description: Abstract We investigate the effective potential and the string tension for the spatial Wilson loop (SWL) in hot dense QGP with two types of anisotropy, i.e. external magnetic field and spatial anisotropy, employing a holographic approach for the heavy quark model.

pmc-10801906.description: ObjectiveThis study aimed to evaluate the effect of trimethylamine oxide (TMAO) on the incidence and prognosis of cerebral infarction.MethodsWe searched PubMed, Embase, and Cochrane databases for all clinical studies on the association of TMAO with cerebral infarction incidence and prognosis from inception to April 2023.

pmc-11515884.title: Population Health Management effectiveness in the primary healthcare setting: a systematic review
pmc-11515884.creator: R McNamara, N Nour, M Mannix, J Browne, S Donohue
pmc-11515884.description: BackgroundPopulation Health Management (PHM) has shown promise as a tool in the improvement of health at scale. It works by; harnessing health-related datasets, allowing for population segmentation and risk stratification, and targeting interventions to yield positive health impact. Prior reviews on PHM, have sought to define PHM and assess feasibility.

pmc-11621451.title: Real-time monitoring of bioelectrical impedance for minimizing tissue carbonization in microwave ablation of porcine liver
pmc-11621451.creator: Xiao Zhang, Wei Wei, Lu Qian, Liuye Yao, Xiaofei Jin, Lidong Xing, Zhiyu Qian
pmc-11621451.description: The charring tissue generated by the high temperature during microwave ablation can affect the therapeutic effect, such as limiting the volume of the coagulation zone and causing rejection. This paper aimed to prevent tissue carbonization while delivering an appropriate thermal dose for effective ablations by employing a treatment protocol with real-time bioelectrical impedance monitoring.

pmc-12356871.title: City-level process-related CO2 emissions in China 2000–2021
pmc-12356871.creator: Sijia Cai, Jinghang Xu, Yuru Guan, Miaomaio Liu, Chang Tan, Jun Bi, Yuli Shan
pmc-12356871.description: As the world’s largest CO2 emitter, China needs accurate city-level CO2 emission accounts to formulate effective low-carbon policies. However, previous studies mainly accounted for emissions from fossil fuel combustion and overlooked process-related CO2 emissions from industrial production (e.g., mineral, chemical, metal products), which account for approximately 13% of China’s total emissions.

pmc-12383275.title: BioFuse: A programmable timer switch of gene expression
pmc-12383275.creator: Cheng Huang, Jie Zhao, Zichun Tan, Shang Dai, Binqiang Wang, Zhenming Xie, Furong Zhang, Yulong Zhou, Ning Yu, Chunhui Cai, Yonghua Yao, Baojun Wang, Bing Tian
pmc-12383275.description: Current gene circuits designed to time gene expression depend on the intricate interactions among various regulators and their targets, which confines them to a limited range of temporal tunability. Here, we report a programmable timer switch of gene expression termed BioFuse, which allows the reaction time ranging from hours to days.
